title: Tiered sampled-cohort pipeline for post-change embedding & reranker verification
creator: Arielle Gomez
description: Build a reproducible, tiered sampling pipeline that runs a suite of offline recall/precision and drift checks whenever a model or key serving configuration (quantization profile, batch size, KV cache policy) is changed. The pipeline should provide fast smoke results for rapid rollouts and deeper cohort analyses for canaries and production rollouts.
background: Current workflow relies on ad-hoc shadow runs and manual sampling when embedding or reranker configs change. This causes slow decision cycles and occasional regressions that reach production. Existing infra (eval harness and synthetic probes) exists but is not orchestrated by config-change events and lacks stratified cohort sampling or tiered time-to-result guarantees.
proposal: Implement a two-tier post-change eval pipeline: (1) QuickSmoke: run lightweight, high-sensitivity probes on a small stratified sample (3k queries) within 10 minutes of a config/model change to detect severe regressions; (2) DeepCohort: run a larger, stratified offline evaluation (50k queries across multiple cohorts and distributions) within 6 hours to surface subtle recall/precision drift and per-cohort breakdowns. Integrate both tiers with the rollout guard so failures block automated promotion.
technical_design: - Triggering: webhook from config manager + model registry on any change to model, quantization, or routing policy. - Sampling: stratified sampling across query length, domain tag, and user cohort; deterministic seed tied to change id for reproducibility. - Metrics: recall@k, precision@k, mean reciprocal rank (MRR), pairwise ranking AUC, embedding cosine drift (mean shift + covariance shift via PSI). - Storage: results persisted to eval-store (time-series + parquet snapshot) and linked to the change id. - Orchestration: Airflow/Argo job templates with QuickSmoke (fast containers, small CT memory) and DeepCohort (larger jobs, multi-shard). - Cost control: cap DeepCohort runs per day per team and leverage cached embedding vectors when model-compatible to reduce compute.
acceptance_criteria: Webhook triggers QuickSmoke within 5 minutes of a config/model change
QuickSmoke completes in <= 15 minutes and produces pass/fail signal based on pre-defined thresholds
DeepCohort completes within 6 hours with cohort-level metrics and per-query examples for any regression
Failing QuickSmoke blocks automated rollout and opens a ticket in Linear with telemetry links
Pipeline can be invoked manually with a change id and reproduces results deterministically
metrics: embedding mean shift (L2) and population stability index (PSI)
alerting_thresholds: QuickSmoke fail: recall@10 drop >= 8% relative to baseline or precision@10 drop >= 6%
DeepCohort fail: any cohort recall@10 drop >= 4% with p-value < 0.01
Embedding drift: PSI > 0.2 or mean shift L2 > configured limit
SLA: QuickSmoke runtime > 30 minutes triggers infra alert
rollout_plan: 1) Prototype QuickSmoke on a sandbox config and validate deterministic sampling. 2) Run DeepCohort against last 5 model changes to sanity-check baselines. 3) Wire webhook and block-policy: QuickSmoke fail => block promotion; DeepCohort fail => auto-create rollback candidate and notify PM/Eng. 4) Start with manual gating for two product teams for one sprint, then enable auto-block for low-risk teams. 5) Post-rollout: iterate thresholds for false positives and add web UI links in Console.
monitoring_playbook: - On QuickSmoke fail: auto-file Linear issue with attached top 50 failing queries, stack trace, and link to job log. Pager only for production branch failures. - On DeepCohort fail: notify SRE/ML-ops channel and schedule triage within 4 hours. - If embedding drift alerts fire repeatedly (>3 times in 24h), pause automated promotions and require human review. - Triage template includes reproduction steps, baseline snapshots, and suggested mitigations (tuning quantization, increase batch size, rollback model).
implementation_notes: Start with copying existing eval harness tests but refactor sampling and result persistence. Add deterministic seeding and expose a --change-id flag. Coordinate with Console team for results surface (cards + diff view). Budget ~120 compute hours for prototype runs. Consider using cached vectors when model family unchanged.
qa_steps: Create a sandbox config change and observe QuickSmoke triggered via webhook
Verify QuickSmoke deterministic seed produces same top-10 regression examples when re-run
Introduce a synthetic regression (e.g., perturb embeddings) and assert QuickSmoke and DeepCohort catch the degradation
Validate permissions so safe-list teams can bypass auto-block during early tests
notes: Keep thresholds conservative to avoid developer friction; instrument false positive tracking so we can tighten thresholds as confidence grows.
